facts.fact: NISR states that the NCI-CRVS system registers nine events including births and deaths, and that 341,029 births and 36,021 deaths occurring in 2024 were registered in it (413,017 births and 42,469 deaths registered in all from January 2024 to end January 2025).
facts.system: National Centralized and Integrated Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (NCI-CRVS) system

facts.fact: NISR states that the national centralised NCI-CRVS captures vital events in real time, directly at the site of occurrence where official registration takes place, as a single data entry point, each registered event being instantly captured in the National Population Registry.
facts.system: National Centralized and Integrated Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (NCI-CRVS) system

facts.fact: NISR states that the paper-based civil registration system was phased out entirely in 2023 after full digitalisation, a physical register being lawful for only six months after the launch of the matching NCI-CRVS module.
facts.system: National Centralized and Integrated Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (NCI-CRVS) system

facts.fact: NISR states that NCI-CRVS was officially launched on 10 August 2020 in all public and private health facilities, on an incremental scale, for the official registration of births and deaths at the place of occurrence.
facts.system: National Centralized and Integrated Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (NCI-CRVS) system

facts.fact: NISR states that all nine NCI-CRVS modules were operational at all relevant registration service points when the 2024 report was compiled: hospitals, health centres, clinics and polyclinics public and private, cells, sectors, districts and embassies; it gives no count of registration points, only the administrative totals of 30 districts, 416 sectors and 2,148 cells.
facts.system: National Centralized and Integrated Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (NCI-CRVS) system

facts.fact: NISR states that the National Identification Agency (NIDA), under the Ministry of ICT, is mandated to supervise and coordinate the civil registration system nationally, with a steering committee chaired by the Permanent Secretary of Local Government.
facts.system: National Centralized and Integrated Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (NCI-CRVS) system

facts.fact: NISR states that the fourth National Strategy for Development of Statistics, running 2024/25 to 2028/29, names strengthening the CRVS system a top priority; NCI-CRVS itself was a recommendation of the first National CRVS Strategic Plan 2017/18-2021/22.
facts.system: National Centralized and Integrated Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (NCI-CRVS) system

facts.fact: NISR credits the financial support of Vital Strategies-Bloomberg Philanthropies Data for Health, UNFPA, WHO and UNICEF as instrumental in enhancing the CRVS system; the report names no domestic budget line.
facts.system: National Centralized and Integrated Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (NCI-CRVS) system

facts.fact: NISR states that Law 71/2024 of 26 June 2024 governing persons and family now regulates civil registration, and that its two ministerial orders, on late and delayed birth registration and on the civil status officer in a health facility, were enacted in March 2025.
facts.system: National Centralized and Integrated Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (NCI-CRVS) system

facts.fact: NISR reports death registration completeness of 46.1% in 2024 (36,021 registered of 78,120 expected), up from 41.8% in 2023, and birth registration completeness of 90.3% (90.0% in 2023), attributing the rise in community deaths registered (54.1% of the total) to decentralised digital registration at cell level.
facts.system: National Centralized and Integrated Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (NCI-CRVS) system
